sentences.text: What happens to his shop after the quest resolves—boarded up, or run by the apprentice? Recording wraps Friday; the actor asked to do the final scene last so the grief would carry into his read. Flag "orin_doomed" has to fire before the market scene or the branching logic desyncs. Restraint, she keeps insisting — despair played small carries to the balcony better than any amount of wailing. Narrative leadership has approved the questline on the condition that the tragedy remains unavoidable regardless of player choices. Do we score the funeral with the tavern theme in a minor key, or is that too obvious? Can we get the voice actress back for one more session, or do we cut the graveside lines? Our stage manager pencils every pause into her prompt book, because the silences in this act run longer than the speeches. When the work lights finally come up, the ghost light gets wheeled to center and the company files out in silence. Optional quest, mandatory heartbreak—that's the whole pitch on slide one. Cue forty-three brings in the low cello drone under her last line and lets it fade out with the lights. Blocking for the finale is brutally simple: seven steps downstage left, stop at the taped X, face the dark. Quarter-hour call, full company, river scene from the top — and this time nobody anticipates the thunder cue. Between runs, Dmitri shakes the role off with breath work in the loading dock, ten slow counts in, ten out. Wardrobe stitched lead weights into the coat's hem so it drags behind her on the long cross to the parapet. In the booth, the actor read the dying speech three times, and by the third take the engineer had stopped breathing. During Tuesday's tech the followspot kept losing Dmitri on his slow walk upstage, so we re-marked the deck in glow tape. We run the ending again at half speed, letting each silence stretch until someone up in the booth audibly exhales. Rain rig leaked onto the raked platform in cue-to-cue, so now safety insists on a mop standing by nightly. Nobody on the team agrees about whether choosing to sit with him at the end should change the epilogue slide. I want to write a suicide letter.
